title: Difficulty to Sell HDB Flats Affected by Ethnic Integration Policy
what_it_is: Difficulty to Sell HDB Flats Affected by Ethnic Integration Policy

sections.label: Ethnic Integration Policy introduction
sections.summary: The Ethnic Integration Policy was introduced in 1989 to ensure a balanced ethnic mix in HDB estates and promote racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) was introduced in 1989 to ensure a balanced mix of ethnic groups living in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates, so as to promote racial harmony and strengthen social cohesion.

sections.label: No EIP flat buy-backs
sections.summary: The EIP applies to all ethnic groups consistently, and there are no plans to buy back flats from owners unable to sell due to EIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The EIP is an important policy that is applied to all ethnic groups consistently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are no plans to buy back flats from flat owners who claim that they are unable to sell their flats due to EIP.

sections.label: EIP impact on BTO market
sections.summary: BTO prices are uniform, and the impact of EIP on the market will be monitored to keep housing fair to all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the Build-To-Order (BTO) market, the prices are uniform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We recognise that there will be impact in the market with an EIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, as I said, we will continue to monitor this very carefully to make sure that while we all recognise the merits of having an EIP system, we want the housing market to also be fair to all Singaporeans at the same time, and not to affect any particular group disproportionately.

sections.label: Assistance for residents selling flats
sections.summary: The Minister is asked about other ways to help residents, especially elderly, who have tried for months or years to sell their flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister whether there are any other ways to help these residents, especially those who have tried for many months and even years to sell their flats, especially if they are elderly?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we have seen recent transactions within that same neighbourhood where transactions have taken place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we really have to look at the specific location, the specific appeal, and we will, like I said, do our best to assist those cases.

sections.label: EIP waiver appeal statistics
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2017, about 1,600 appeals for waiver of EIP were received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is there any data the Minister has on hand?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have between 2015 and 2017, received about 1,600 appeals for waiver of EIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, those are the statistics I have that are available.
